blocks.text: Exercise 1. a) bēti · bitha · bitna · b) ʾōḍtak · ʾoḍithum · c) abūya · abūki · d) aḫūh · aḫūna · e) šaʾʾiti · šaʾʾitkum · f) mirātu · g) ʿarabiyyiti · h) ṣaḥbi · ṣaḥbaha Exercise 2. a) bitāʿ Lūka (also: bitāʿu) · b) aywa, btaʿti · c) btūʿ Yāsmīn · d) laʾ, miš bitaʿtiof btāʿit Hudā · e) aywa, bitaʿna · f) aywa, bitūʿi Exercise 3. a) ʿammi · b) ḫālti · c) giddi (giddu) · d) ibn ʿammiti · e) ḥamāti · f) gōz uḫti (There is not one word; is also heard nasībi (My brother-in-law) g) giddites (tēta) · h) ʿammu Exercise 4. a) ʾōḍtak fēn? · b) of ʿarabiyyiti. (also: l-ʿarabiyya btaʿti.) · c) mirāt aḫūya maṣriyya. · d) šaʾʾitna f d-dōr it-tālit. · e) ʿandi aḫḫēn w-uḫt. (also: itnēn iḫwāt wi-uḫt.) · f) il-kitāb from bitāʿak? · g) tēta Sakna. maʿāna. · h) maʿāya muftāḥ il-bēt. Exercise 5 · Example. šaʾʾiti f Milānu, fi ḥayy ʾurayyib mi-l-maḥaṭṭa. hiyya fi d-dōr ir-rābiʿ, wi-l-ʿimāra fīha asansēr, il-ḥamdu li-llāh. iš-šaʾʾa fīha ʾōḍa wi-ṣāla wi-maṭbaḫ ṣuġayyar wi-ḥammām. f ʾōḍit in-nōm fīh sirīr wi- dulāb wi-maktab, wi-l-laptop bitāʿi dayman ʿalē. f ṣ-ṣāla fīh kanaba w-tarabēza. il-balakōna btaʿti ṣuġayyara bass bataḥibbha ʾawi. iš-šaʾʾa miš wasʿa, bass nḍīfa w-hadya. hiyya igār, wi-l-igār ġāli šuwayya. Hadya is quiet. Exercise 6 · Example of tree. Umm Šarīf (māma) • his children Šarīf (engineering student in Milan) and Yāsmīn (Student of Economy in Cairo) · Umm's brother Šarīf, ḫāl Ḥusām, with his wife ṭanṭ Hāla and three children (the cousins of Šarīf) · Grandma (tēta), which lives on the second floor of the same building. The family lives in Shubra, on the fifth floor. Exercise 7. 1. Nādīn · in Heliopolis (Maṣr il-Gidīda) · a large apartment, three bedrooms and a living room · parents, a younger brother studying medicine, grandmother · grandmother has lived with them for two years and her room is next to that of Nādīn. 2. ʿAmr · in Giza, the Pyramids area (the-Haram), on the third floor · a rented apartment, a bit tight · the wife and two daughters · are married for five years and would like to buy a larger apartment near his work. 3. il-ḥagga Ṣafiyya · in a house in the country, in Upper Egypt · a family home · children all married, seven grandchildren · at each feast all the family goes to her and the house is filled. Exercise 8. a) Pictures of their house in Shubra, sent to their mother. You sit down in the afternoon and drink tea. One is of Šarīf (with the desk he was studying in high school) Yāsmīn (full of economics books). The uncle of Šarīf, brother of the mother: for this reason it is ḫāl; on ʿamm is the father's brother. Every Friday, lunch at Grandma's. Grandma on the second floor, Šarīf and his family on the fifth. b) The bag, blue. His Arabic book. Her class: the teacher Salmā and the comrades. The eldest son is an engineer in Dubai, the minor still studies at the university in Minya, his daughter is married and has three children. In the village, in Minya, in their home. A two-storey country house with a small garden; Luca's has only one room and a living room. Unit verification. 1. ʿarabiyyiti · il-ʿarabiyya btaʿti · 2. ʾoḍitha · 3. šaʾʾitna · 4. aḫūya · 5. abūkum · 6. the kutub of btūʿ mīn? · 7. iš-šanṭa of miš bitaʿtiof btaʿtik. · 8. maʿāya l-mafatīḥ. · 9. ḫāli · 10. mirāt Ḥusām · 11. tēta Sakna. maʿāna. · 12. il-bēt fīh talat ʾowaḍ wi-balakōna. · 13. iš-šaʾʾa igār, fi d-dōr ir-rābiʿ. · 14. ibn ʿammi Mitgawwiz. · 15. What's your (bag)? · 16. My eldest son is an engineer. · 17. My wife (the lady) is in the country. · 18. The apartment is a little tight. · 19. I was studying in my room. · 20. He has three children. For parts A and B by voice, the tutor accepts the suffix or bitāʿ where both are possible; removes the point for bitāʿ with a kinship name, for ʿamm in place of ḫāl and for the forms of fuṣḥā (abī, ġurfatī).
